cards.explanation: The answer is lack. David says, "The LORD is my shepherd; I shall not want." To not want means to lack nothing he needs. I spent years in a junk drawer lacking a whole list of things, friends, and light was at the top. David's shepherd leaves nothing off the list.

The answer is rest and peace. David says, "He makes me lie down in green pastures; He leads me beside quiet waters." Lying down and quiet water. That's a picture of rest and peace, friends. After my drawer years, I can tell you that sounds like a vacation.

The answer is restores. David says, "He restores my soul…" Restore means to bring back, to set right again. I know a little about being worn down, friends, and getting set right again is a gift. This part of the care goes deeper than grass and water.

The answer is for the sake of His name. David says, "He guides me in the paths of righteousness for the sake of His name." Notice whose name it is, friends: the LORD's. David's reason for being guided points straight to the LORD Himself.

The answer is because the LORD is with him. David says, "…I will fear no evil, for You are with me…" That's his reason. The valley didn't change, but he isn't walking it alone. Walking a dark hallway by yourself is one thing, and walking it with somebody beside you is another.

The answer is True. David says, "Your rod and Your staff, they comfort me." A big stick in a dark valley could scare you, but David finds comfort in it. I think that's because the shepherd is holding it. Whatever else is in that valley, the comfort is real.
The answer is table. David says, "You prepare a table before me…" The picture is a host setting a table for a guest. Getting ready for someone is a way of saying they matter.

The answer is False. David says, "You prepare a table before me in the presence of my enemies." Not far from them, friends, but in their presence. The enemies are part of the scene, and the table is still prepared for David.

The answer is that he has more than enough. David says, "my cup overflows." A cup that spills over is holding more than it needs, and I think that's the picture he wants you to see. He's got more than enough, and he knows where it came from. That's a good thing to be able to say.

The answer is goodness and mercy. David says, "Surely goodness and mercy will follow me all the days of my life…" They follow him, friends, and not just on a good day. It says all the days. That's a lot of days for good things to keep up.

The answer is in the house of the LORD. David ends with, "…I will dwell in the house of the LORD forever." Dwell means he stays there, and forever means no end date. After all those years in a drawer I was waiting to be let out, friends. David's last line is about being welcomed in to stay.
